title: TRACE-HEOR: proposed ten item standard for Transparent Reporting of Artificial intelligence Components in health Economics and Outcomes Research
footnote: TRACE-HEOR is designed as an extension to CHEERS 2022 and PALISADE rather than as a replacement, and is aligned to the FDA credibility assessment framework and to ELEVATE-GenAI. Items 1, 2, 6, 9, and 10 constitute the minimum set. Item 6 is the item no current instrument requires and the item a reimbursement committee needs most. Every item is stated so that it can be verified by a reviewer with access only to the submission.
rows: Declare, for each AI component, which function it performed: evidence identification or screening, data extraction, cohort or exposure definition, outcome or endpoint derivation, covariate or confounder selection, effect estimation, parameter derivation, model code generation, synthetic data or external control generation, or narrative drafting. Name the model, version, vendor, and dates of use.
Disclosure instruments currently ask whether AI wrote the text. Disclosed AI use was 3 of 1,391 HTA documents (0.2%) and 0.6% of Lancet submissions, against self reported use of 25% to 69%.
Context of use and model risk
State the question of interest, the context of use, and the model risk using the two factor definition of model influence and decision consequence, and name the decision the model influences.
Adopts the FDA credibility assessment framework verbatim so that a single characterisation serves both regulatory and HTA review.
Report calibration in the deployment population and time period, not only discrimination. Where the estimate depends on absolute risk or absolute cost, discrimination alone is insufficient.
Across four deployed clinical AI systems, calibration degraded earlier and more consistently than discrimination. Cost effectiveness results depend on calibration.
Where AI output is validated against human abstraction, report the reliability of that human reference, including inter-abstractor agreement.
The reference standard for scaled machine learning response abstraction itself had agreement of 0.94 on assessment presence and 0.82 on best response category.
Report performance separately for each variable the analysis depends on. Aggregate F1 or accuracy is not sufficient.
Stage value reached 98.8% precision while histology linkage reached 79% recall in the same model; T stage reached F1 0.89 while M stage reached 0.24.

Re-estimate the primary result with the AI component replaced by the pre-AI alternative or by a plausible worst case, and state whether the incremental cost effectiveness ratio crosses the relevant threshold or whether the recommendation changes.
No existing instrument requires this. Deriving real-world progression from radiology reports rather than clinical notes moved median survival by seven months, which is decision relevant.
Report performance for the subgroups the decision affects, and report the demographic composition of any training or synthetic population.
A commercial risk algorithm applied to approximately 200 million people identified 17.7% of Black patients for extra help where a corrected target identified 46.5%.
Report generator family, fidelity against the real target quantity rather than against summary statistics, and a privacy evaluation.
Generator choice alone moved recovery of the true median progression free survival from 6.5% to 98.1% of replicates. Only 11% of studies used a differentially private generator.
Report quantitatively what fraction of AI output was reviewed, by whom, with what qualifications, and what the disagreement rate was.
A biased AI lowered clinician diagnostic accuracy by 11.3 percentage points and explanations did not protect; experienced radiologists fell from 82.3% to 45.5% with an incorrect suggestion.
Deposit prompts, code, model versions, random seeds, and intermediate outputs in a citable archive at the time of submission.
Five percent of health economic evaluations mention code availability. An AI assisted analysis is not auditable without the prompts.
